Sliding-window median in O(log k) per step

Recomputing the median of a window by sorting it again for every new element costs O(k log k) per step. Keeping the window in two heaps, a max-heap for the lower half and a min-heap for the upper half, gives O(log k) per step: push the new element onto one heap, move the top between heaps so that their sizes differ by at most one, and read the median from the top of the larger heap.

Elements that leave the window are not searched for. Instead they are counted in a dictionary of pending deletions and discarded lazily when they reach the top of either heap, so each step stays logarithmic and the median is exactly the one the sorting version returns.

Complexity

For a window of k elements over n inputs the two-heap method takes O(n log k) time and O(k) extra memory, against O(n k log k) for sorting every window.
